decisions.reason: The candidate already has a message-73 MODIFY capturing the independently stated requirement that bowls lift out without obstruction from the whisk or motor assembly; the quick whisk-removal change requires no additional candidate-state change.
Quick, simple whisk detachment for cleaning and swapping does not change the independent requirement that spout components be removable for cleaning.
The source changes whisk-removal usability and does not alter how the spout or liquid path must be flushed or cleaned.
Whisk detachment speed, complexity, and tool use do not affect the bottom-seal requirement for preventing liquid ingress into electronics.
The message's splash-control language reiterates the existing higher-speed splash constraint and existing mitigation options; the whisk-removal modification adds no new splash-control state.

Quick tool-free whisk removal does not change the established smooth, frothy, and high-speed mixing-quality criteria; the message's height-specific outcome is already owned by the whisk-positioning requirement.
The whisk-removal usability change does not necessarily alter the enclosure's size or side-profile constraints.
The source preserves the existing design direction and introduces no change to the DJ-inspired visual identity.
Quick whisk detachment does not necessarily change the unit's base support, rigidity, or resistance to rattling and shifting.

The candidate already has a message-73 INTRODUCE capturing the independently stated whisk-height requirement for foam quality and splash control; no additional positioning change follows from the removal modification.
The source changes the whisk attachment's removal behavior, not the whisk head's size, material, or selected mixing design.
The quick-removal requirement does not change the approved maximum speed, continuous-operation restriction, or supported speed modes.
